response: ## Accessibility Issue: Image missing alternative text (WCAG 1.1.1) **Bug ID:** `A11Y-7c2d9e4a` (instance) / `A11Y-f3b8a1c5` (pattern) **URL:** https://news.example.com/articles/spring-garden-guide **XPath:** `//article[@class='feature-story']/img[@class='hero']` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/main/article[@class='feature-story']/img[@class='hero']` **WCAG SC:** 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A) **Rule:** axe-core — image-alt **Severity:** Critical **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page; appears across all article pages using the `article.feature-story` template ### HTML Snippet ```html ``` ### Description The hero image inside the featured story article lacks any form of alternative text. It has no `alt` attribute, no `aria-label`, and is not marked up as decorative (`role="presentation"` or `role="none"`). Screen reader users receive no information about the image's content when navigating past it. For a news site where visual context matters for understanding article relevance, this omission removes meaningful content from the experience of blind and low-vision users. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://news.example.com/articles/spring-garden-guide 2. Open NVDA (or VoiceOver on macOS) 3. Use arrow keys or Tab to move through page content until reaching the hero image near the top of the article 4. Observe that the screen reader announces only "graphic" with no descriptive text ### Expected Behaviour Screen reader should announce a meaningful description of the image, such as: *"Spring garden guide — blooming tulips and vegetable seedlings"* (or equivalent alt text describing the visual content). If the image is purely decorative, it should be marked up so assistive technologies skip it entirely. ### Actual Behaviour Screen reader announces only "graphic" with no accompanying label or description. The `` element has no `alt` attribute and no ARIA attributes to provide an accessible name. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Chrome 126.0.0.0 | | OS | macOS 14.5 | | Screen reader | VoiceOver (built-in) / NVDA if available on Windows | | Zoom level | 100% | | Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 | ### Impact Blind and low-vision users relying on screen readers cannot access the visual context provided by this hero image, which may contain important information about the article topic (e.g., identifying plants shown in a gardening guide). Users of voice control software also cannot reference or interact with an unnamed graphic element. ### Suggested Fix ```html ```
